criterion: harmful = the extra element produces a consequence (unreachable/dead-end/absorbing/conflicting-target/preemption/semantic shift) that can be stated as ONE POSITIVE assertion drawn only from the consequence predicates (reaches / terminates / occupancy_after / initial_target / stays_in / event_consumed / cardinality / containment / guard_distinguishable / invariant / persists_until / response_within / variable_delta_after) and that assertion evaluates False on the FCSTM projection. Existence predicates (state_/edge_/event_/variable_/action_/effect_declared) are the PREMISE for an extra, never the defect. No closed-world reading: 'NL never mentioned it' is not harm, and 'NL never forbade it' is not innocence.

items.element: extra PumpControl.InitialState (4th direct substate, absorbing, and it is the only [*] target inside PumpControl)
items.consequence: NL06 s2 enumerates exactly three substates ('there are three main substates: PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState'). The extra state makes the direct non-pseudo child count 4, and because `[*] -> InitialState` is PumpControl's only initial edge the extra state also captures the entry and is itself a dead end (no outgoing edge), so all three NL-named substates become unreachable.

items.note: cardinality is a FRESH assertion for this pair: 0002#0 (problem) uses initial_target and 0002#1 (problem) uses reaches, so it does not double-book. The reviewer's `assertable` was already cardinality and is correct.
